findings.claim: The attribute is emitted behind `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no exclusion. The requirement says all generated code should be decorated. The README documents this limit, but generated code for those targets still skews coverage. Also, ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists in netstandard2.0 for types (it was added in .NET Framework 4.0 / netstandard2.0), so the guard may be unnecessary.

findings.claim: The change modifies EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces output: the brace is now `{\r\n` when constraints exist. This is unrelated to the requirement and alters generated formatting for nested generic types. L4 records that nesting and constraint logic has had many recent fixes.
